idea: 023 Aggressive order flow absorbed: taker-buy share against the block's own return (scout idea 9)
hypothesis: On bitcoin and ether, a 4-hour block in which aggressive buyers take an unusually large share of the volume (z of the taker-buy share over the last 180 blocks >= +1.5) while the block's price did not rise (close <= open) predicts a fall over the next 12 hours; an unusually low taker-buy share (z <= -1.5) with a price that did not fall (close >= open) predicts a rise.
mechanism: Signed volume read as absorption: when market orders on one side dominate and the price does not move their way, a large passive (limit) trader is absorbing them and the price tends to move the other way once the aggressors stop. Signed (taker) volume is information the lab's 118 crypto price-only configurations never used. A fade on a flow imbalance, not one of the closed price-only families.

data.signal: Binance spot 1h klines BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT (kit.data.binance_klines(sym, '1h'), data.binance.vision monthly dumps, columns volume and taker_buy_base), 2017-08-17 .. 2021-12-31, every hour including weekends (Binance trades 24/7). Blocks = 4-hour UTC blocks starting 00, 04, 08, 12, 16, 20 UTC, built from their 4 hourly klines (a block missing an hour or with zero volume is dropped). b = sum taker_buy_base / sum volume over the block; r = close of the last hour / open of the first hour - 1. z = (b - mean) / std over the last W valid blocks including the current one (rolling W rows, at least 70 % of W), past only. A block's b, r and z are KNOWN at the block's end (block open + 4 h = open of its last kline + 1 h).
data.publication_lag: none: exchange klines are final at the candle's close and never revised; a value is used from its block's end, never earlier
data.prices: kit.data.load_bars('btcusd') and load_bars('ethusd') = Binance BTCUSDT / ETHUSDT 1h (price_is mid), FP's crypto closure (Fri 23:55 to Mon 00:00 server) removed by the kit; costs FP's btcusd / ethusd
data.in_sample_years: 2017-08-17 .. 2021-12-31 (4.4 years); power check from the signal data alone (power.py / power.json): main = 140 BTC and 133 ETH signal blocks, 128 + 125 = 253 entries with one position per market and a 12 h hold; the basket route (no n bar on a basket; one market cannot reach 250)

rule_main.signal: at each block end t with W = 180: short if z >= +1.5 and r <= 0; long if z <= -1.5 and r >= 0. Only blocks that START Monday to Friday (UTC) and whose end t lies outside FP's crypto closure (kit.data.fp_closed): the brief's 'weekdays' on FP's clock. known_at = t.
rule_main.side: -1 when buyers dominate without a rise (z >= +thr, r <= 0); +1 when sellers dominate without a fall (z <= -thr, r >= 0)
rule_main.entry: open of the first H1 bar opening at or after known_at (the next block's open; delay 0, max_wait_h = 2)
rule_main.overlap: one position per market (kit.sim mode 'one'); every-signal variant for the every-signal bar

what_changed_vs_brief: Stop: the brief's '2 x the mean 4-hour range of the last 30 blocks' cannot be given to kit.sim (stops are d20 or bps). Translated to ('d20', 0.7): the median ratio of 2 x mean(4h high-low over 30 blocks) to the kit's D20, measured on ranges only (no return, no trade outcome) over 2017-2021, is 0.698 (BTC) and 0.707 (ETH) (cache script stop_ratio.py). The z window counts blocks on all days (crypto trades 24/7); signals only on weekday blocks outside FP's closure. My count (140 / 133) differs from the scout's (151 / 144), probably because the scout did not remove blocks ending in FP's closure (Friday evening) or counted the z window differently: written, not chased.
costs: kit.costs (FP Raw, crypto btcusd / ethusd): gross, net, spread and slippage x1.5
bars: CHARTER.md 'The bars' on 01_main as a BASKET of 2 markets (small-basket amendment: no market above 75 % of the profit), computed by kit.judge.verdict; t on daily sums of R; random-entry null 2000 draws (same-day for legs decided together); weekly corr with the ten <= 0.30; deflated Sharpe on N_all (N_main reported). Gross, net, long and short sides and each market reported apart.
